note: Synthetic session invented for tests (Toyota Echo, rear-left bearing, then an intermittent ABS light after a hub replacement). It mirrors the shape of an old export: float likelihoods, string flags and a synthetic 'Please continue' user turn at message 3. No real person's data.

state.title: Bumpy-road ABS light after new hub
safety_flags: Do not reuse the old hub nut: it is normally a one-use nut; fit a new one and tighten it to the specified torque
Verify the new hub nut was torqued to specification; an under-torqued hub can shift and damage the wheel end. Do not drive until checked
If the new hub shows play or makes noise, stop driving and have it checked
With the ABS light on, anti-lock braking may be disabled; the ordinary brakes still work, so leave longer gaps
Reconnect the ABS sensor fully after testing until it clicks
Support the rear on jack stands on flat ground; never work under a car held only by a jack

suspected_causes.cause: ABS sensor connector half-latched or a terminal disturbed during the hub work
suspected_causes.evidence: The light started after the sensor was unplugged and flickers on rough roads.
suspected_causes.next_check: Reseat the connector until it clicks and inspect both halves for corrosion or a bent pin.

suspected_causes.cause: ABS sensor wire strained near the new hub
suspected_causes.evidence: A new hub can pull or twist the flexible wire; a broken strand shows up over bumps.
suspected_causes.next_check: Trace the wire from the hub and look for a missing clip or a rub mark.

suspected_causes.cause: Sensor air gap or tone ring on the new hub
suspected_causes.evidence: A new hub brings a new tone ring; a sensor not fully seated changes the signal.
suspected_causes.next_check: Pull the sensor, clean its tip and check the ring for grit.

messages.content: there is a rhythmic humming from the rear of the car between 30 and 50 km/h. it gets louder in long left bends
A hum from the rear that changes in bends often points at a wheel bearing. Lift one rear wheel at a time and spin it by hand: listen and feel for roughness. Which wheel is louder?
I lifted both rear wheels and spun them. the left one feels gritty and sounds like the hum, the right is smooth
Please continue from my last saved message. Do not repeat it.
A gritty rear-left wheel points at its bearing. Next, take the wheel off and spin only the hub: if the roughness stays, the bearing is the cause.
wheel off and spinning only the hub, it is rough once per revolution
That confirms a worn rear-left bearing. Replace the hub assembly, torque the new hub nut to the specified figure and do not reuse the old nut.
I replaced the hub. now the ABS light flickers on and off
After hub work an intermittent ABS light usually points at the wheel speed sensor connector, its wiring, or the sensor seating. Reseat the connector first.
Bump-triggered flicker fits a half-latched connector or a strained sensor wire near the new hub. Check both before suspecting the sensor itself.
it is a new wheel hub on the car
Then the sensor air gap and the tone ring on the new hub are worth checking too: look for grit, paint or a sensor that is not fully seated.
